outcome: Intention to have a vaginal birth
cohort: 222 primiparous women visiting a healthcare center in Khorram Abad, Iran
finding: Intention to have a vaginal birth was significantly correlated with awareness of childbirth methods, perceived sensitivity to childbirth complications, perceived intensity of childbirth pain, perceived barriers and benefits of vaginal birth, and self-efficacy for vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Perceived barriers to vaginal birth were the strongest predictor of childbirth type, followed by awareness of childbirth methods.
